rows.speaker: Antonius
rows.current: "That's why I have money." I looked around the cheap office.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: "I know that now." Rusk laughed again. Antonius ignored him.

rows.speaker: Rusk
rows.previous: Rusk looked interested. Antonius did not react. I continued.
rows.current: "You already remember patterns. Son wants out. Hidden lender. Bad order. Temporary shortage. Structural problem. Write the reason when you refuse. Six months later, see whether you were right." Antonius stared. I felt the branches trying to come.
rows.following: Categories. Default models. Industry risk. Borrower types. Information network.

rows.speaker: Arlo
rows.current: "Yours sounds expensive." Antonius sat again.

rows.speaker: Antonius
rows.current: "Yes." Arlo looked at me.

rows.speaker: Antonius
rows.current: "Maybe." Arlo looked between us. "You're becoming unbearable in the same direction."

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: "Fine." I looked at Arlo. "Anything?" I asked.

rows.speaker: Arlo
rows.previous: "Can we test function without feeding it mana?" I asked.
rows.current: Arlo said, "Maybe mechanically." He opened the wrist clasp. The inside leather had hardened with age, but beneath it were tiny metal contacts arranged around the forearm. Not armor. Definitely not armor. Arlo whistled softly. Antonius said, "Good whistle or expensive whistle?"

rows.speaker: Antonius
rows.current: "Maybe." Arlo looked between us. "You're becoming unbearable in the same direction."

rows.speaker: Then
rows.previous: "Did you do magic with the boxes?" I stopped.
rows.current: "How could you possibly know that?" Rusk smiled.
rows.following: "You told me you cast Barrier, then I sent you to move something heavy. You're Greg."

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: "Then learn that while making one." Arlo stared at me. I enjoyed this far too much.

rows.speaker: Antonius
rows.current: "That you can protect yourself from very poor assassins." I stopped.

rows.speaker: almost
rows.current: "Which finger?" I stared at her.

rows.speaker: almost
rows.current: "Good." I held up my hand.

rows.speaker: almost
rows.current: "How will you know?" I looked at the outside of the cup. No marks.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: "Liar." Hessa smiled.
rows.following: I picked up the cup again. Weight. Height. I could measure with my finger.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.current: "Nearly sixty." Hessa stared at me. Then laughed. One short sound. Not amused.

rows.speaker: GREG
rows.previous: I thought of the Chronoclast. Cold metal. Wrongness. Then this room. Not this room. My old room. Young body. No back pain.
rows.current: "I touched something." Hessa stared.

rows.speaker: Jalen
rows.previous: Jalen nodded toward the storehouse doors.
rows.current: “You came here first.” I walked another six minutes. The freight yard occupied a broad packed-earth square inside the west wall where carts could be weighed, split, reloaded, inspected, delayed, taxed, cursed, and occasionally repaired.
rows.following: Today it was mostly cursed. Rain had made the center soft. Not mud everywhere. Worse. Mud in specific places. Deep wheel ruts cut through the traffic lane. Three loaded carts waited along the wall. A fourth sat crooked near the weighing platform with its left rear wheel removed. Crates occupied the ground beside it under two canvas sheets. A teamster shouted at a yard clerk.

rows.speaker: Alden
rows.previous: Sova said, “If Pip sees it again, my problem.” Good. Pig looked at us. I had known kings with less confidence.
rows.current: There was a farmhouse maybe two hundred yards through the orchard. Smoke. Someone home. Alden said, “I'll tell them.” He crossed the ditch. Pessa said, “I'll keep carts.” Dorn kept dog. Sova returned to oil. I had no assigned role. Excellent. Pig started climbing toward road. There. I stepped sideways. It stopped. I stepped closer. It changed direction. I knew nothing about pigs.
rows.following: Future Greg had fought boar-shaped things. Not same. I spread my arms. Pig turned. Good.

rows.speaker: Driver
rows.previous: Related. Not opposite. The box dried enough. New wax. Seal. Done. We took the north bridge. This added distance. Sevren did not complain. At bridge midpoint, a wagon blocked half the span. Rear axle tilted. Driver underneath. Two farmhands standing. No danger. Just obstruction. Sevren looked at gap between wagon and rail. Maybe three feet. Enough for people. Not cart. We were people.
rows.current: He went through. I followed. Driver said, “Watch the wheel.” Sevren stepped around. I stepped around. No intervention. Excellent. On far side, one farmhand called, “Courier.” Sevren turned.
